source.text: וַיִּצָּעֵק֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר צָפ֑וֹנָה וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ לְיִפְתָּ֜ח מַדּ֣וּעַ׀עָבַ֣רְתָּ׀לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בִּבְנֵי־עַמּ֗וֹן וְלָ֨נוּ֙ לֹ֤א קָרָ֨אתָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת עִמָּ֔ךְ בֵּיתְךָ֕ נִשְׂרֹ֥ף עָלֶ֖יךָ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And were called out [the] men of Ephraim and crossed to Zaphon, and they said to Jephthah, why did you cross over to fight against [the] sons of Ammon, and us not you called to go with you? Your house we will burn over you with fire.

en.L: And the men of Ephraim were called out, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight against the sons of Ammon and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire."
en.B: The men of Ephraim were called to arms, and they crossed over to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites and not call us to go along? We will burn your house over your head!"
en.R: The men of the tribe of Ephraim gathered their army and crossed the Jordan River to the town of Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, "Why did you go to fight the Ammonites and not call us to go with you? We are going to burn your house down with you inside it!"

sw.L: Nao watu wa Efraimu wakaitwa, wakavuka hadi Zafoni, wakamwambia Yeftha, "Kwa nini ulivuka kwenda kupigana na wana wa Amoni, wala hukutuita sisi twende pamoja nawe? Tutaichoma nyumba yako juu yako kwa moto."
sw.B: Watu wa Efraimu waliitwa vitani, wakavuka mpaka Zafoni. Walimwambia Yeftha, "Kwa nini ulivuka kwenda kupigana na Waamoni bila kutuita twende pamoja nawe? Tutaiteketeza nyumba yako ukiwa ndani yake!"
sw.R: Watu wa kabila la Efraimu walikusanya jeshi lao, wakavuka Mto Yordani mpaka mji wa Zafoni. Walimwambia Yeftha, "Kwa nini ulikwenda kupigana na Waamoni bila kutuita twende pamoja nawe? Tutaichoma nyumba yako, nawe ukiwa ndani yake!"

es.L: Y fueron convocados los hombres de Efraín, y pasaron a Zafón y dijeron a Jefté: «¿Por qué pasaste a pelear contra los hijos de Amón y no nos llamaste para ir contigo? Quemaremos tu casa sobre ti con fuego».
es.B: Los hombres de Efraín fueron llamados a las armas y pasaron a Zafón. Le dijeron a Jefté: «¿Por qué pasaste a pelear contra los amonitas y no nos llamaste para ir contigo? ¡Vamos a quemar tu casa contigo dentro!».
es.R: Los hombres de la tribu de Efraín reunieron su ejército, cruzaron el río Jordán y llegaron al pueblo de Zafón. Le dijeron a Jefté: «¿Por qué fuiste a pelear contra los amonitas y no nos llamaste para ir contigo? ¡Vamos a quemar tu casa contigo adentro!».

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Éphraïm furent convoqués, et ils passèrent à Tsaphôn et dirent à Jephté : « Pourquoi es-tu passé pour combattre contre les fils d’Ammon, et ne nous as-tu pas appelés pour aller avec toi ? Nous brûlerons ta maison sur toi par le feu. »
fr.B: Les hommes d’Éphraïm furent appelés aux armes et passèrent à Tsaphôn. Ils dirent à Jephté : « Pourquoi es-tu allé combattre les Ammonites sans nous appeler à marcher avec toi ? Nous allons brûler ta maison sur ta tête ! »
fr.R: Les hommes de la tribu d’Éphraïm ont rassemblé leur armée et ils ont traversé le Jourdain jusqu’à la ville de Tsaphôn. Ils ont dit à Jephté : « Pourquoi es-tu allé combattre les Ammonites sans nous appeler pour venir avec toi ? Nous allons brûler ta maison avec toi dedans ! »

vi.L: Những người Ép-ra-im được triệu tập, và họ đi qua đến Xa-phôn và nói với Giép-thê: "Sao ông đi qua đánh con cái Am-môn mà không gọi chúng tôi cùng đi với ông? Chúng tôi sẽ lấy lửa đốt nhà ông cùng với ông."
vi.B: Những người Ép-ra-im được triệu tập ra trận, và họ đi qua đến Xa-phôn. Họ nói với Giép-thê: "Sao ông đi qua đánh người Am-môn mà không gọi chúng tôi cùng đi? Chúng tôi sẽ đốt nhà ông, thiêu cả ông ở trong đó!"
vi.R: Những người thuộc chi tộc Ép-ra-im tập hợp quân đội và vượt sông Giô-đanh đến thành Xa-phôn. Họ nói với Giép-thê: "Sao ông đi đánh người Am-môn mà không gọi chúng tôi cùng đi? Chúng tôi sẽ đốt nhà ông với ông ở trong đó!"

ko.L: 에브라임 사람들이 소집되어 사본으로 건너가서 입다에게 말했다. "너는 어찌하여 암몬 자손과 싸우러 건너가면서 우리를 불러 너와 함께 가게 하지 않았느냐? 우리가 네 집을 너와 함께 불로 태워 버리겠다."
ko.B: 에브라임 사람들이 싸우려고 모여서 사본으로 건너갔다. 그들이 입다에게 말했다. "너는 왜 암몬 사람들과 싸우러 건너가면서 우리를 불러 함께 가자고 하지 않았느냐? 우리가 네 집을 너와 함께 불태워 버리겠다!"
ko.R: 에브라임 지파 사람들이 군대를 모아 요단강을 건너 사본 성으로 갔다. 그들이 입다에게 말했다. "너는 왜 암몬 사람들과 싸우러 가면서 우리를 불러 함께 가자고 하지 않았느냐? 우리가 네 집에 불을 질러 너까지 태워 버리겠다!"

decisions.choice: the men of Ephraim were called out: Ephraim mustered for war, angry at being left out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Ephraim was called out to join Gideon's pursuit (7:23-24), and Ephraim's complaint repeats its quarrel with Gideon (8:1). Gideon calmed them with gentle words (8:2-3); Jephthah will answer them very differently. The men of Ephraim saw being left out of a war as an insult to their tribe's honor, and perhaps as a loss of their share of the spoil.

decisions.choice: crossed to Zaphon: to a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The word can be the name of the town Zaphon, in the Jordan valley in the land of Gad (Joshua 13:27), or the common noun "north" with the ending meaning "toward", giving "crossed northward". Ephraim lived west of the Jordan and Jephthah east of it, so the men must have crossed the river eastward; a town on the east bank fits that better than a direction. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: burn your house over you with fire: a threat to kill Jephthah and his household
decisions.reason: To burn a man's house over him was to destroy him and his family together. The Philistines made the same threat to Samson's wife (14:15) and carried it out (15:6).

decisions.choice: were called to arms; Readable "gathered their army", "the Jordan River", "the town of"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the men of Ephraim were called together as an army. Readable also names the river they crossed and says that Zaphon is a town.

decisions.choice: "Tsaphôn"; "Éphraïm", "les Éphraïmites"
decisions.reason: Names with no established French form are transcribed from the Hebrew as in the Pentateuch, with "ts" for tsade; the circumflex marks the long o, as in "Nahshôn". The same rule gives Ibtsân, Élôn, Ayyalôn, Abdôn and Piratôn below. Ephraim keeps its usual French form.

decisions.choice: "Ép-ra-im" for Ephraim, "Xa-phôn" for Zaphon
decisions.reason: Ephraim keeps the form of the Genesis note; Zaphon, a name not used before in Vietnamese, takes the usual Protestant spelling and stays the same through the block.

decisions.choice: The men of Ephraim and Jephthah speak to each other in the plain style (해라체) with "너" and "너희"
decisions.reason: Two angry sides of the same people face each other as equals; the plain style carries the threat and the reply.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִפְתָּח֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֣ישׁ רִ֗יב הָיִ֛יתִי אֲנִ֛י וְעַמִּ֥י וּבְנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן מְאֹ֑ד וָאֶזְעַ֣ק אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־הוֹשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם אוֹתִ֖י מִיָּדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jephthah to them, [a] man of strife I was, I and my people and [the] sons of Ammon, greatly; and I called you, and not you saved me from their hand.

en.L: And Jephthah said to them, "I was a man of great strife, I and my people, with the sons of Ammon; and I called you, and you did not save me from their hand.
en.B: Jephthah answered them, "My people and I were in a bitter struggle with the Ammonites. I called you, but you did not rescue me from their power.
en.R: Jephthah answered them, "My people and I were having a terrible fight with the Ammonites. I called for your help, but you did not come and save me from them.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akawaambia, "Mimi nilikuwa mtu wa ugomvi mkubwa, mimi na watu wangu, pamoja na wana wa Amoni; nami niliwaita, lakini hamkuniokoa kutoka mkononi mwao.
sw.B: Yeftha aliwajibu, "Mimi na watu wangu tulikuwa katika mapambano makali na Waamoni. Niliwaita, lakini hamkuniokoa kutoka mikononi mwao.
sw.R: Yeftha aliwajibu, "Mimi na watu wangu tulikuwa katika vita vikali na Waamoni. Niliwaita mje kunisaidia, lakini hamkuja kuniokoa kutoka kwao.

es.L: Y Jefté les dijo: «Hombre de gran contienda fui yo, yo y mi pueblo, con los hijos de Amón; y {{plural_you:los|os}} llamé, y no me {{plural_you:salvaron|salvasteis}} de su mano.
es.B: Jefté les respondió: «Mi pueblo y yo estábamos en una dura lucha con los amonitas. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} llamé, pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no me {{plural_you:libraron|librasteis}} de su poder.
es.R: Jefté les contestó: «Mi pueblo y yo estábamos en una pelea terrible con los amonitas. Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} pedí ayuda, pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no {{plural_you:vinieron|vinisteis}} a salvarme de ellos.

fr.L: Et Jephté leur dit : « J’étais un homme de grande querelle, moi et mon peuple, avec les fils d’Ammon ; et je vous ai appelés, et vous ne m’avez pas sauvé de leur main.
fr.B: Jephté leur répondit : « Mon peuple et moi, nous étions en lutte acharnée avec les Ammonites. Je vous ai appelés, mais vous ne m’avez pas délivré de leur pouvoir.
fr.R: Jephté leur a répondu : « Mon peuple et moi, nous avions une terrible bataille contre les Ammonites. Je vous ai appelés à l’aide, mais vous n’êtes pas venus me sauver.

vi.L: Giép-thê nói với họ: "Tôi và dân tôi đã có cuộc tranh chiến lớn với con cái Am-môn; tôi đã gọi các ông, nhưng các ông không cứu tôi khỏi tay chúng.
vi.B: Giép-thê đáp: "Tôi và dân tôi đã phải chiến đấu gay go với người Am-môn. Tôi đã gọi các ông, nhưng các ông không giải cứu tôi khỏi tay chúng.
vi.R: Giép-thê trả lời họ: "Tôi và dân tôi đã đánh nhau dữ dội với người Am-môn. Tôi đã kêu các ông giúp đỡ, nhưng các ông không đến cứu tôi khỏi chúng.

ko.L: 입다가 그들에게 말했다. "나와 내 백성이 암몬 자손과 크게 다투는 사람이 되었을 때에, 내가 너희를 불렀으나 너희는 나를 그들의 손에서 구원하지 않았다.
ko.B: 입다가 그들에게 대답했다. "나와 내 백성은 암몬 사람들과 큰 싸움을 하고 있었다. 내가 너희를 불렀지만 너희는 나를 그들의 손에서 건져 주지 않았다.
ko.R: 입다가 그들에게 대답했다. "나와 내 백성은 암몬 사람들과 아주 힘든 싸움을 하고 있었다. 내가 너희에게 도와 달라고 했지만, 너희는 와서 나를 구해 주지 않았다.

decisions.choice: a man of great strife: deep in a serious conflict
decisions.reason: "A man of strife" is someone caught up in a dispute. Here it covers both the argument Jephthah carried on with the king of Ammon (11:12-28) and the war that followed it.

decisions.choice: I called you, and you did not save me: Jephthah's reply to Ephraim's charge
decisions.reason: Ephraim said that Jephthah did not call them (verse 1); Jephthah says that he did, and they did not come. Chapter 11 does not tell of this call, so the reader has only Jephthah's word for it.

decisions.choice: from their hand: from their power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control, as often (2:14, 16, 18).

decisions.choice: rescue / come and save
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the judges whom the LORD raises to save Israel (2:16, 18). Balanced says "rescue"; Readable adds "come and", since the complaint is that Ephraim did not come.

source.text: וָֽאֶרְאֶ֞ה כִּֽי־אֵינְךָ֣ מוֹשִׁ֗יעוָאָשִׂ֨ימָה נַפְשִׁ֤י בְכַפִּי֙ וָֽאֶעְבְּרָה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדִ֑י וְלָמָ֞ה עֲלִיתֶ֥ם אֵלַ֛י הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I saw that not you [were] saving, and I put my life in my palm and crossed over to [the] sons of Ammon, and gave them Yahweh into my hand; and why have you come up to me the day the this to fight against me?

en.L: And when I saw that you were not saving [me], I put my life in my palm and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into my hand. And why have you come up to me this day to fight against me?"
en.B: When I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to me. So why have you come up against me today to fight with me?"
en.R: When I saw that you were not going to help, I risked my life and went across to fight the Ammonites. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let me defeat them. So why have you come here today to fight against me?"

sw.L: Nami nilipoona ya kuwa hamniokoi, niliweka uhai wangu katika kiganja changu, nikavuka kwenda kwa wana wa Amoni, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mkononi mwangu. Basi kwa nini mmepanda kunijia siku hii ya leo kupigana nami?"
sw.B: Nilipoona kwamba hamtaniokoa, niliyahatarisha maisha yangu, nikavuka kwenda kupigana na Waamoni, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mikononi mwangu. Basi kwa nini mmepanda leo kunishambulia na kupigana nami?"
sw.R: Nilipoona kwamba hamtakuja kunisaidia, niliyahatarisha maisha yangu, nikavuka kwenda kupigana na Waamoni. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniwezesha kuwashinda. Basi kwa nini mmekuja hapa leo kupigana nami?"

es.L: Y cuando vi que no [me] {{plural_you:salvaban|salvabais}}, puse mi vida en mi mano y pasé contra los hijos de Amón, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en mi mano. ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:han subido|habéis subido}} hoy contra mí para pelear conmigo?».
es.B: Cuando vi que no me {{plural_you:iban|ibais}} a salvar, arriesgué mi vida y pasé a pelear contra los amonitas, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me los entregó. ¿Por qué, entonces, {{plural_you:han subido|habéis subido}} hoy a pelear contra mí?».
es.R: Cuando vi que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no me {{plural_you:iban|ibais}} a ayudar, arriesgué mi vida y crucé para pelear contra los amonitas. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dejó vencerlos. ¿Por qué {{plural_you:vienen|venís}} hoy a pelear contra mí?».

fr.L: Et quand j’ai vu que vous ne [me] sauviez pas, j’ai mis ma vie dans ma paume et je suis passé vers les fils d’Ammon, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a livrés dans ma main. Et pourquoi êtes-vous montés vers moi ce jour-ci pour combattre contre moi ? »
fr.B: Quand j’ai vu que vous ne me sauveriez pas, j’ai risqué ma vie et je suis passé combattre les Ammonites, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me les a livrés. Pourquoi donc êtes-vous montés contre moi aujourd’hui pour me faire la guerre ? »
fr.R: Quand j’ai vu que vous n’alliez pas m’aider, j’ai risqué ma vie et je suis allé combattre les Ammonites. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a permis de les vaincre. Alors pourquoi êtes-vous venus aujourd’hui pour me combattre ? »

vi.L: Khi tôi thấy các ông không cứu [tôi], tôi đã liều mạng sống mình trong lòng bàn tay và đi qua đánh con cái Am-môn, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phó chúng vào tay tôi. Vậy sao hôm nay các ông lại lên đây đánh tôi?"
vi.B: Khi thấy các ông không cứu tôi, tôi đã liều mạng đi qua đánh người Am-môn, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phó chúng vào tay tôi. Vậy tại sao hôm nay các ông lại kéo lên đây để đánh tôi?"
vi.R: Khi thấy các ông sẽ không giúp, tôi đã liều mạng vượt sông đánh người Am-môn. Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho tôi thắng chúng. Vậy sao hôm nay các ông lại đến đây đánh tôi?"

ko.L: 너희가 [나를] 구원하지 않는 것을 보고, 나는 내 목숨을 내 손바닥에 두고 암몬 자손에게로 건너갔고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 내 손에 넘겨주셨다. 그런데 어찌하여 너희가 오늘 나에게 올라와 나와 싸우려 하느냐?"
ko.B: 너희가 나를 구하지 않으리라는 것을 알고, 나는 목숨을 걸고 암몬 사람들과 싸우러 건너갔다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 내 손에 넘겨주셨다. 그런데 너희는 왜 오늘 나를 치러 올라와 나와 싸우려 하느냐?"
ko.R: 너희가 나를 도와주지 않을 것을 알고, 나는 목숨을 걸고 암몬 사람들과 싸우러 건너갔다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내가 그들을 이기게 해 주셨다. 그런데 너희는 왜 오늘 여기까지 와서 나와 싸우려 하느냐?"

decisions.choice: I put my life in my palm: I risked my life
decisions.reason: To hold one's life in one's hand is to put it at risk, as in 1 Samuel 19:5; 28:21; Job 13:14. Jephthah means that he went to war alone, without Ephraim's help, at the risk of his own life.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave them into my hand: the victory came from the LORD
decisions.reason: "Gave into my hand" is the usual way Judges speaks of victory as the LORD's gift (3:28; 4:14; 7:9; 11:32). Jephthah credits the LORD, which also tells Ephraim that they have no claim on the victory.

decisions.choice: why have you come up against me: a question that is also a reproach
decisions.reason: The question is a rebuke: Ephraim stayed away from the danger but now comes armed against the one who faced it.

decisions.choice: [me]
decisions.reason: The participle "saving" has no object in the Hebrew; Literal supplies "me" from verse 2.

decisions.choice: risked my life; let me defeat them
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the two pictures (life in the palm; given into the hand) in plain words.

decisions.choice: "niliyahatarisha maisha yangu" (I risked my life) at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "niliweka uhai wangu katika kiganja changu"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew picture of holding one's life in one's palm (m1) is not a Swahili saying, so Balanced and Readable give its sense; Literal keeps the picture so the reader can see the idiom.

decisions.choice: "puse mi vida en mi mano" (L); "arriesgué mi vida" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture ("in my palm", said in Spanish "en mi mano"); Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1), as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And gathered Jephthah all [the] men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim, and struck [the] men of Gilead Ephraim, because they said, fugitives of Ephraim [are] you, Gilead, in [the] midst of Ephraim, in [the] midst of Manasseh.

en.L: And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they had said, "You [are] fugitives of Ephraim, Gilead, in the midst of Ephraim, in the midst of Manasseh."
en.B: Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The men of Gilead defeated Ephraim, because the Ephraimites had said, "You Gileadites are nothing but runaways from Ephraim, living among Ephraim and Manasseh."
en.R: So Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, and they fought against the men of Ephraim and beat them. The men of Ephraim had insulted them. They had said, "You people of Gilead are only runaways from Ephraim. You live among the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, but you do not really belong."

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akawakusanya watu wote wa Gileadi, akapigana na Efraimu, nao watu wa Gileadi wakampiga Efraimu, kwa sababu walikuwa wamesema, "Ninyi [ni] wakimbizi wa Efraimu, Gileadi, katikati ya Efraimu, katikati ya Manase."
sw.B: Kisha Yeftha aliwakusanya watu wote wa Gileadi, akapigana na Efraimu. Watu wa Gileadi wakawashinda Waefraimu, kwa sababu Waefraimu walikuwa wamesema, "Ninyi Wagileadi si kitu ila watoro wa Efraimu, mnaoishi kati ya Efraimu na Manase."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yeftha aliwakusanya watu wote wa Gileadi, nao wakapigana na watu wa Efraimu, wakawashinda. Watu wa Efraimu walikuwa wamewatukana. Walikuwa wamesema, "Ninyi watu wa Gileadi ni watoro tu kutoka Efraimu. Mnaishi kati ya makabila ya Efraimu na Manase, lakini hamna nafasi halisi kati yao."

es.L: Y reunió Jefté a todos los hombres de Galaad y peleó contra Efraín; y los hombres de Galaad hirieron a Efraín, porque [ellos] habían dicho: «Fugitivos de Efraín [son] {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, Galaad, en medio de Efraín, en medio de Manasés».
es.B: Entonces Jefté reunió a todos los hombres de Galaad y peleó contra Efraín. Los hombres de Galaad derrotaron a Efraín, porque los efraimitas habían dicho: «{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los galaaditas, no {{plural_you:son|sois}} más que fugitivos de Efraín que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} entre Efraín y Manasés».
es.R: Así que Jefté reunió a todos los hombres de Galaad, y pelearon contra los hombres de Efraín y los vencieron. Los de Efraín los habían insultado. Les habían dicho: «{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los de Galaad, no {{plural_you:son|sois}} más que fugitivos de Efraín. {{plural_you:Viven|Vivís}} entre las tribus de Efraín y Manasés, pero en realidad no {{plural_you:son|sois}} de aquí».

fr.L: Et Jephté rassembla tous les hommes de Galaad et combattit contre Éphraïm, et les hommes de Galaad frappèrent Éphraïm, parce qu’ils avaient dit : « Vous [êtes] des fugitifs d’Éphraïm, Galaad, au milieu d’Éphraïm, au milieu de Manassé. »
fr.B: Alors Jephté rassembla tous les hommes de Galaad et livra bataille à Éphraïm. Les hommes de Galaad battirent Éphraïm, car les Éphraïmites avaient dit : « Vous, les Galaadites, vous n’êtes que des fuyards d’Éphraïm, qui vivez au milieu d’Éphraïm et de Manassé. »
fr.R: Jephté a donc rassemblé tous les hommes de Galaad. Ils ont combattu les hommes d’Éphraïm et ils les ont battus. Les hommes d’Éphraïm les avaient insultés. Ils avaient dit : « Vous, les gens de Galaad, vous n’êtes que des fuyards d’Éphraïm. Vous vivez au milieu des tribus d’Éphraïm et de Manassé, mais vous n’êtes pas vraiment de chez nous. »

vi.L: Giép-thê tập hợp tất cả những người Ga-la-át và đánh Ép-ra-im, và những người Ga-la-át đánh bại Ép-ra-im, vì [người Ép-ra-im] đã nói: "Các ngươi, Ga-la-át, [là] những kẻ trốn chạy của Ép-ra-im, ở giữa Ép-ra-im, ở giữa Ma-na-se."
vi.B: Rồi Giép-thê tập hợp tất cả những người Ga-la-át và đánh Ép-ra-im. Người Ga-la-át đánh bại Ép-ra-im, vì người Ép-ra-im đã nói: "Bọn Ga-la-át các ngươi chỉ là những kẻ trốn chạy khỏi Ép-ra-im, sống giữa Ép-ra-im và Ma-na-se."
vi.R: Vậy Giép-thê tập hợp tất cả những người Ga-la-át, và họ đánh người Ép-ra-im và thắng. Người Ép-ra-im đã sỉ nhục họ. Họ đã nói: "Dân Ga-la-át các ngươi chỉ là những kẻ trốn chạy khỏi Ép-ra-im. Các ngươi sống giữa các chi tộc Ép-ra-im và Ma-na-se, nhưng thật ra không thuộc về đâu cả."

ko.B: 입다는 길르앗 사람들을 모두 모아 에브라임과 싸웠다. 길르앗 사람들은 에브라임을 무찔렀다. 에브라임 사람들이 "너희 길르앗 사람들은 에브라임과 므낫세 사이에 얹혀사는 에브라임의 도망자들일 뿐이다" 하고 말했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 입다는 길르앗 사람들을 모두 모았다. 그들은 에브라임 사람들과 싸워 그들을 이겼다. 에브라임 사람들이 전에 그들을 모욕했기 때문이다. 에브라임 사람들은 "너희 길르앗 사람들은 에브라임에서 도망쳐 나온 자들일 뿐이다. 너희는 에브라임과 므낫세 지파 사이에 살지만, 진짜로 거기에 속한 사람들이 아니다" 하고 말했었다.

decisions.choice: fugitives of Ephraim: an insult saying that the Gileadites were deserters with no proper place of their own
alternatives: you Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim, living between Ephraim and Manasseh
decisions.reason: The sense of the saying is not certain. It seems to mock the people of Gilead as runaways who had fled from Ephraim and lived on the edges of Ephraim and Manasseh, not as a true tribe of their own. Jephthah himself had been driven out of his family (11:1-3), which may sharpen the insult. The Hebrew is short and hard to read.

decisions.choice: fugitives of Ephraim: the insult is turned back on those who spoke it
decisions.reason: The same words, "fugitives of Ephraim", come again in verse 5, where they are the defeated Ephraimites trying to escape across the river. The ones who mocked others as runaways become runaways themselves.

decisions.choice: Gilead, Ephraim, Manasseh: tribes on both sides of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Half of Manasseh had settled in Gilead east of the Jordan and half lay west of the river next to Ephraim (Numbers 32:39-40; Joshua 17:1-10). Ephraim and Manasseh were both sons of Joseph, so the quarrel is within one family of tribes.

decisions.choice: the Ephraimites had said; Readable "had insulted them", "but you do not really belong"
decisions.reason: Balanced names the speakers so that it is clear who said the insult. Readable says plainly that it was an insult and spells out what it seems to mean; that expansion follows one understanding of a hard saying.

decisions.choice: The Ephraimites' insult uses "các ngươi" and, at B, "bọn"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks contempt through the pronoun; the insult (meaning decision) is carried by "các ngươi" rather than the polite "các ông" of the earlier exchange.

decisions.choice: captured the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim: cut off the Ephraimites' way home
decisions.reason: The fords were the shallow places where the Jordan could be crossed on foot. Holding them trapped the beaten Ephraimites on the east side, away from their own land. Ehud and Gideon used the same tactic against Moab and Midian (3:28; 7:24); now Israelites use it against Israelites.

decisions.choice: Ephraimite: a man of the tribe of Ephraim
decisions.reason: The word can also mean someone from Ephrathah, the clan around Bethlehem (Ruth 1:2; 1 Samuel 17:12), but here, as in 1 Samuel 1:1 and 1 Kings 11:26, it means a member of the tribe of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: and it was that whenever: a scene that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The opening words describe what took place each time a fugitive came to the river, not a single event. The sentence runs on into verse 6.

decisions.choice: Whenever one of the Ephraimites who were escaping said / Whenever an Ephraimite ... came and said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the fugitives" (plural) and then "to him" (singular). Balanced and Readable make the whole scene about one man at a time. Readable adds why the fords mattered.

decisions.choice: "Mwefraimu", plural "Waefraimu", for a man of Ephraim; "Wagileadi" for the men of Gilead
decisions.reason: Swahili names a member of a tribe or people with the prefixes m- and wa- (as "Mwisraeli", "Waisraeli"); the place and tribe names themselves keep their usual form, "Efraimu" and "Gileadi".

decisions.choice: The fleeing Ephraimites speak in the 하오체 ("주시오", "아니오") at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: A stranger asking to cross, trying not to give himself away, speaks neither down nor humbly; the guards answer in the plain style.

sw.L: ndipo walipomwambia, "Sema basi, 'Shibolethi.'" Naye akasema, "Sibolethi," kwa kuwa hakuweza kulitamka sawasawa. Nao wakamkamata, wakamchinja kwenye vivuko vya Yordani. Na wakaanguka wakati huo wa Efraimu 42,000.
sw.B: walimwambia, "Basi sema 'Shibolethi.'" Naye alisema "Sibolethi," kwa sababu hakuweza kulitamka neno hilo sawasawa. Ndipo walipomkamata na kumwua pale kwenye vivuko vya Yordani. Wakati huo Waefraimu 42,000 walianguka.

es.L: le decían: «Di ahora “Shibolet”». Y él decía: «Sibolet», y no lograba pronunciar[la] bien. Y lo agarraban y lo degollaban junto a los vados del Jordán. Y cayeron en aquel tiempo de Efraín 42 000.

fr.R: ils lui disaient : « Alors dis “Shibboleth”. » S’il disait « Sibboleth », ils savaient qu’il était d’Éphraïm, parce que les gens d’Éphraïm ne pouvaient pas dire ce mot comme il faut. Alors ils l’attrapaient et le tuaient là, au passage de la rivière. Cette fois-là, 42 000 hommes d’Éphraïm ont été tués.

ko.L: 그들이 그에게 "자, '쉽볼렛' 하고 말해 보아라" 하고 말했다. 그가 '십볼렛' 하고 말하며 바르게 말하지 못하면, 그들이 그를 붙잡아 요단 나루터에서 죽였다. 그때에 에브라임 사람 사만 이천 명이 쓰러졌다.

decisions.choice: Shibboleth / Sibboleth: a test word that gave away a man's accent
decisions.reason: The two words differ only in their first sound, "sh" against "s". The people of Ephraim evidently said "s" where the people of Gilead said "sh", so asking a man to say the word showed where he came from. The word itself is an ordinary noun, meaning "ear of grain" (Genesis 41:5) or "stream, flowing water" (Psalm 69:3, 16); at a river crossing the second sense may have been in mind. What mattered was not its meaning but its sound, so both words are given as they sound, not translated.

decisions.choice: he could not manage to say it right: he was unable to make the sound
decisions.reason: The verb means to prepare or set in order; with "not" it says that the man did not get the word right, or could not manage it. The point is that the accent gave him away even when he tried.

decisions.choice: slaughtered him: killed him without mercy
decisions.reason: The verb is often used of slaughtering animals. It shows a cold execution of men who were trying to flee, not deaths in battle.

decisions.choice: forty-two thousand: a very large loss for one tribe
decisions.reason: "Thousand" is kept here, as in the census of Numbers 1. The word can also name a military or clan unit, which would give a much smaller number (see the note at Numbers 1).

decisions.choice: Shibboleth, Sibboleth
decisions.reason: Every level gives the two words in letters that show their sound, since the story turns on how they were said. Readable adds "they knew he was from Ephraim" to explain what the test showed.

decisions.choice: men of Ephraim; the river crossing
decisions.reason: Readable says "men of Ephraim" since those killed were the fighters fleeing the battle, and "river crossing" for "fords".

decisions.choice: "Shibolethi" and "Sibolethi", the test word in a Swahili spelling that keeps the sh / s difference
alternatives: translating the word ("suke", an ear of grain)
decisions.reason: The point of the test is the sound, not the meaning (m1), so the word is kept, with the Swahili final vowel; Swahili writes "sh" and "s" as English does, so the difference stays visible.

decisions.choice: "Shibolet" and "Sibolet"
decisions.reason: The test word is transliterated so that Spanish readers hear the two sounds that gave the speaker away (m1): "sh" and "s". Spanish has no "sh" sound of its own, but readers know it from borrowed words, and the contrast must be heard. Numbers follow the English: figures where it has figures, with a space for thousands ("42 000") as in Numbers.

decisions.choice: numbers above a hundred in figures, with a no-break space for thousands ("42 000"); "[hommes]" supplied at Literal
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21: as the French style guide sets, numbers are written in words up to "cent" and in figures above, as the Pentateuch drafts write "603 550". Literal supplies "[hommes]", which French needs after the number and the Hebrew leaves implied.

decisions.choice: "Si-bô-lết" and "Xi-bô-lết"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese spelling keeps the two sounds apart with "s" and "x", which many speakers still pronounce differently, so the reader can see the difference the test turned on.

decisions.choice: "쉽볼렛" and "십볼렛"
decisions.reason: The test turns on one sound, "sh" against "s". Korean writes the two as "쉽" and "십", which keeps the difference audible to a Korean reader.

decisions.choice: judged Israel: led and governed Israel
decisions.reason: As at 2:16, a judge was a leader raised up to rescue Israel and govern it, more than a judge in a court.

decisions.choice: in the cities of Gilead: buried in a town of Gilead
alternatives: in his town, Mizpah of Gilead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural "cities", which is odd for one burial place. The ancient Greek translation reads "in his city, in Gilead", which needs only a small change in the Hebrew letters; Jephthah's home was Mizpah of Gilead (11:34). The Hebrew text is kept, understood as a burial in one of Gilead's towns.

decisions.choice: six years: a short rule with no years of peace
decisions.reason: Jephthah's notice gives no period when "the land had peace", unlike Othniel, Ehud, Deborah and Gideon (3:11, 30; 5:31; 8:28). His story closes with the deaths of his daughter (11:39) and of many Ephraimites.

decisions.choice: one of the towns of Gilead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "one of the towns", since a man is buried in one place; Literal keeps the plural as written. Readable says "led" for "judged", as at 2:16.

decisions.choice: "aliwaamua Israeli" (judged Israel) at Literal and Balanced; "aliwaongoza Israeli" (led Israel) at Readable; the leaders are "waamuzi"
decisions.reason: As agreed for Judges in every language: "kuamua" keeps the link with "mwamuzi", the title of these leaders; Readable says what they did, lead the people, as the English Readable "led Israel" does.

decisions.choice: "juzgó a Israel" (L, B); "dirigió a Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21, as the terms note sets: the Hebrew verb is "judged", which Literal and Balanced keep; Readable says "dirigió", since the judges led and governed Israel and did more than settle cases in court (m1).

decisions.choice: "jugea Israël" (L, B); "a dirigé Israël" (R)
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21, as the terms note for these books sets: the verb keeps the link with the title "juge" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says what the judges did, leading and governing Israel (m1), as the English Readable says "led".

decisions.choice: "xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L, B), "lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note sets for *shafat*: the judges were leaders who rescued and governed Israel (meaning decision), so Readable says plainly that they led.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘을 다스렸다" at Literal and Balanced; "이스라엘을 이끌었다" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for the verb "judge" in Judges: the judges led and governed Israel, more than deciding court cases.

decisions.choice: Bethlehem: either the town in Judah or the town of the same name in Zebulun
decisions.reason: The text does not say which Bethlehem is meant. Elsewhere Judges names Bethlehem of Judah (17:7; 19:1), but there was also a Bethlehem in Zebulun (Joshua 19:15), and the next judge, Elon, is from Zebulun (verse 11). Either is possible.

decisions.choice: Ibzan, Elon and Abdon: three short notices of leaders

ko.L: 그에게는 아들 서른 명이 있었다. 그는 딸 서른 명을 밖으로 보냈고, 밖에서 딸 서른 명을 자기 아들들을 위하여 데려왔다. 그는 칠 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.B: 그에게는 아들 서른 명과 딸 서른 명이 있었다. 그는 딸들을 자기 씨족 밖으로 시집보냈고, 밖에서 젊은 여자 서른 명을 데려와 아들들의 아내로 삼았다. 그는 칠 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.

decisions.choice: sent outside / brought from outside: arranged marriages beyond his own clan
decisions.reason: To "send" a daughter is to give her away in marriage, and to "bring in" daughters for sons is to take wives for them. "Outside" means outside Ibzan's own clan. By marrying his sixty children into other families he joined his house to many others.

decisions.choice: thirty sons and thirty daughters: a large and powerful household
decisions.reason: So many children meant many wives and great wealth, the sign of a man of high rank, like Jair with his thirty sons (10:4) and Gideon with his seventy (8:30).

decisions.choice: gave ... in marriage; clan / family group; young women; as wives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the sending and bringing were marriages. The Hebrew says "daughters" both times; Balanced and Readable say "young women" the second time, since these were not Ibzan's own daughters.

fr.B: Puis Ibtsân mourut et fut enterré à Bethléem.
fr.R: Puis Ibtsân est mort, et on l’a enterré à Bethléem.

vi.L: Íp-xan qua đời và được chôn tại Bết-lê-hem.
vi.B: Rồi Íp-xan qua đời và được chôn tại Bết-lê-hem.
vi.R: Rồi Íp-xan qua đời và được chôn tại Bết-lê-hem.

ko.B: 그 뒤에 입산은 죽어서 베들레헴에 묻혔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 입산은 죽어서 베들레헴에 묻혔다.

decisions.choice: buried in Bethlehem: in his home town
decisions.reason: Ibzan was buried in the town he came from (verse 8). Which Bethlehem is meant is discussed there.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ט אַֽחֲרָיו֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵיל֖וֹן הַזְּבֽוּלֹנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And judged after him Israel Elon the Zebulunite, and he judged Israel ten years.

en.L: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.
en.B: After him, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel. He judged Israel for ten years.
en.R: After Ibzan, a man named Elon led Israel. He was from the tribe of Zebulun, and he led Israel for ten years.

sw.L: Na baada yake Eloni Mzabuloni akawaamua Israeli, naye akawaamua Israeli miaka kumi.
sw.B: Baada yake, Eloni Mzabuloni aliwaamua Israeli. Aliwaamua Israeli kwa miaka kumi.
sw.R: Baada ya Ibzani, mtu aitwaye Eloni aliwaongoza Israeli. Alitoka katika kabila la Zabuloni, naye aliwaongoza Israeli kwa miaka kumi.

es.L: Y después de él juzgó a Israel Elón el zabulonita; y juzgó a Israel diez años.
es.B: Después de él, Elón el zabulonita juzgó a Israel. Juzgó a Israel durante diez años.
es.R: Después de Ibzán, un hombre llamado Elón dirigió a Israel. Era de la tribu de Zabulón, y dirigió a Israel durante diez años.

fr.L: Et après lui, Élôn le Zabulonite jugea Israël, et il jugea Israël dix ans.
fr.B: Après lui, Élôn le Zabulonite jugea Israël. Il jugea Israël pendant dix ans.
fr.R: Après Ibtsân, un homme appelé Élôn a dirigé Israël. Il était de la tribu de Zabulon, et il a dirigé Israël pendant dix ans.

vi.L: Sau ông, Ê-lôn người Sa-bu-lôn xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên mười năm.
vi.B: Sau ông, Ê-lôn người Sa-bu-lôn xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên trong mười năm.
vi.R: Sau Íp-xan, một người tên là Ê-lôn lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông thuộc chi tộc Sa-bu-lôn, và ông lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên mười năm.

ko.L: 그 뒤에 스불론 사람 엘론이 이스라엘을 다스렸다. 그는 십 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.B: 입산 뒤에 스불론 사람 엘론이 이스라엘을 다스렸다. 그는 십 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.R: 입산 다음에는 엘론이라는 사람이 이스라엘을 이끌었다. 그는 스불론 지파 사람이었고, 십 년 동안 이스라엘을 이끌었다.

decisions.choice: Elon the Zebulunite: from the tribe of Zebulun in the north
decisions.reason: Zebulun's land lay in lower Galilee, north of the valley of Jezreel (Joshua 19:10-16). Elon is also the name of one of Zebulun's sons (Genesis 46:14; Numbers 26:26), so this judge bears an old family name of his tribe.

decisions.choice: After Ibzan; from the tribe of Zebulun
decisions.reason: Readable names Ibzan for "him", explains "the Zebulunite", and says "led" for "judged", as at 2:16.

source.text: וַיָּ֖מָת אֵל֣וֹן הַזְּבֽוּלֹנִ֑י וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּאַיָּל֖וֹן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ זְבוּלֻֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And died Elon the Zebulunite and was buried in Aijalon in [the] land of Zebulun.

en.L: And Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
en.B: Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
en.R: Then Elon died and was buried in the town of Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

sw.L: Naye Eloni Mzabuloni akafa, akazikwa Aiyaloni katika nchi ya Zabuloni.
sw.B: Kisha Eloni Mzabuloni alikufa, akazikwa Aiyaloni katika nchi ya Zabuloni.
sw.R: Kisha Eloni alikufa, akazikwa katika mji wa Aiyaloni katika nchi ya Zabuloni.

es.L: Y murió Elón el zabulonita y fue sepultado en Ajalón, en la tierra de Zabulón.
es.B: Después Elón el zabulonita murió y fue sepultado en Ajalón, en la tierra de Zabulón.
es.R: Después Elón murió y fue sepultado en el pueblo de Ajalón, en la tierra de Zabulón.

fr.L: Et Élôn le Zabulonite mourut et fut enterré à Ayyalôn, dans le pays de Zabulon.
fr.B: Puis Élôn le Zabulonite mourut, et il fut enterré à Ayyalôn, dans le pays de Zabulon.
fr.R: Puis Élôn est mort, et on l’a enterré dans la ville d’Ayyalôn, dans le pays de Zabulon.

vi.L: Ê-lôn người Sa-bu-lôn qua đời và được chôn tại A-gia-lôn trong xứ Sa-bu-lôn.
vi.B: Rồi Ê-lôn người Sa-bu-lôn qua đời và được chôn tại A-gia-lôn trong xứ Sa-bu-lôn.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-lôn qua đời và được chôn tại thành A-gia-lôn trong xứ Sa-bu-lôn.

ko.L: 스불론 사람 엘론이 죽어 스불론 땅 아얄론에 묻혔다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 스불론 사람 엘론은 죽어서 스불론 땅 아얄론에 묻혔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 엘론은 죽어서 스불론 땅에 있는 아얄론 성에 묻혔다.

decisions.choice: Elon ... Aijalon: the names sound alike
decisions.reason: Without vowels, the names Elon and Aijalon are written with the same letters. The town seems to share its name with the judge, or the two names were linked.

decisions.choice: Aijalon in the land of Zebulun: not the better-known Aijalon
decisions.reason: The best-known Aijalon lay in the west, in the land given to Dan (Joshua 10:12; 19:42). The words "in the land of Zebulun" show that a different place in the north is meant. Its site is not known.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט אַחֲרָ֖יו אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַבְדּ֥וֹן בֶּן־הִלֵּ֖ל הַפִּרְעָתוֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And judged after him Israel Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite.

en.L: And after him Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
en.B: After him, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
en.R: After Elon, a man named Abdon led Israel. He was the son of Hillel, from the town of Pirathon.

sw.L: Na baada yake Abdoni mwana wa Hileli Mpirathoni akawaamua Israeli.
sw.B: Baada yake, Abdoni mwana wa Hileli Mpirathoni aliwaamua Israeli.
sw.R: Baada ya Eloni, mtu aitwaye Abdoni aliwaongoza Israeli. Alikuwa mwana wa Hileli, kutoka mji wa Pirathoni.

es.L: Y después de él juzgó a Israel Abdón hijo de Hilel, el piratonita.
es.B: Después de él, Abdón hijo de Hilel, el piratonita, juzgó a Israel.
es.R: Después de Elón, un hombre llamado Abdón dirigió a Israel. Era hijo de Hilel, del pueblo de Piratón.

fr.L: Et après lui, Abdôn, fils de Hillel, le Piratonite, jugea Israël.
fr.B: Après lui, Abdôn, fils de Hillel, le Piratonite, jugea Israël.
fr.R: Après Élôn, un homme appelé Abdôn a dirigé Israël. C’était le fils de Hillel, de la ville de Piratôn.

vi.L: Sau ông, Áp-đôn con trai Hi-lên, người Phi-ra-thôn, xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Sau ông, Áp-đôn con trai Hi-lên, người Phi-ra-thôn, xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Sau Ê-lôn, một người tên là Áp-đôn lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông là con trai của Hi-lên, đến từ thành Phi-ra-thôn.

ko.L: 그 뒤에 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들 압돈이 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.B: 엘론 뒤에 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들 압돈이 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.R: 엘론 다음에는 압돈이라는 사람이 이스라엘을 이끌었다. 그는 힐렐의 아들이었고, 비라돈 성 출신이었다.

decisions.choice: the Pirathonite: from Pirathon in Ephraim
decisions.reason: Pirathon was a town in the hill country of Ephraim (verse 15). Benaiah, one of David's mighty men, came from there too (2 Samuel 23:30). So after the slaughter of verse 6, a man of Ephraim leads Israel.

decisions.choice: After Elon; from the town of Pirathon
decisions.reason: Readable names Elon for "him", explains "the Pirathonite", and says "led" for "judged", as at 2:16.

source.text: וַיְהִי־ל֞וֹ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים בָּנִ֗ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁים֙ בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים רֹכְבִ֖ים עַל־שִׁבְעִ֣ים עֲיָרִ֑ם וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were to him forty sons and thirty sons of sons riding on seventy donkeys; and he judged Israel eight years.

en.L: And he had forty sons and thirty sons of sons riding on seventy donkeys. And he judged Israel eight years.
en.B: His forty sons and thirty grandsons rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.
en.R: Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons, and each of them rode his own donkey. He led Israel for eight years.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa na wana arobaini na wana wa wana thelathini waliopanda punda sabini. Naye akawaamua Israeli miaka minane.
sw.B: Wanawe arobaini na wajukuu wake thelathini walipanda punda sabini. Aliwaamua Israeli kwa miaka minane.
sw.R: Abdoni alikuwa na wana arobaini na wajukuu thelathini, na kila mmoja wao alipanda punda wake mwenyewe. Aliwaongoza Israeli kwa miaka minane.

es.L: Y tuvo cuarenta hijos y treinta hijos de hijos que montaban sobre setenta asnos. Y juzgó a Israel ocho años.
es.B: Sus cuarenta hijos y treinta nietos montaban en setenta asnos. Juzgó a Israel durante ocho años.
es.R: Abdón tuvo cuarenta hijos y treinta nietos, y cada uno de ellos montaba su propio burro. Dirigió a Israel durante ocho años.

fr.L: Et il eut quarante fils et trente fils de fils, qui montaient sur soixante-dix ânons. Et il jugea Israël huit ans.
fr.B: Ses quarante fils et ses trente petits-fils montaient soixante-dix ânons. Il jugea Israël pendant huit ans.
fr.R: Abdôn avait quarante fils et trente petits-fils, et chacun d’eux avait son propre âne. Il a dirigé Israël pendant huit ans.

vi.L: Ông có bốn mươi con trai và ba mươi cháu trai cưỡi trên bảy mươi con lừa. Ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên tám năm.
vi.B: Bốn mươi con trai và ba mươi cháu trai của ông cưỡi bảy mươi con lừa. Ông xét xử Y-sơ-ra-ên trong tám năm.
vi.R: Áp-đôn có bốn mươi con trai và ba mươi cháu trai, và mỗi người đều cưỡi lừa riêng. Ông lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên tám năm.

ko.L: 그에게는 아들 마흔 명과 아들의 아들 서른 명이 있었는데, 그들은 나귀 일흔 마리를 타고 다녔다. 그는 팔 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.B: 그의 아들 마흔 명과 손자 서른 명은 나귀 일흔 마리를 타고 다녔다. 그는 팔 년 동안 이스라엘을 다스렸다.
ko.R: 압돈에게는 아들 마흔 명과 손자 서른 명이 있었는데, 그들은 저마다 자기 나귀를 타고 다녔다. 그는 팔 년 동안 이스라엘을 이끌었다.

decisions.choice: riding on seventy donkeys: a mark of rank and wealth
decisions.reason: Leaders and their families rode donkeys (5:10; 10:4). Seventy sons and grandsons, each with his own mount, show a large and wealthy household. Seventy is also the number of Gideon's sons (8:30) and of Abimelech's brothers (9:5).

decisions.choice: grandsons
decisions.reason: "Sons of sons" is the Hebrew way of saying grandsons. Readable says "each of them rode his own donkey" for the seventy matching the seventy riders.

decisions.choice: "cháu trai" at Literal for "sons of sons"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has one plain word for a grandson; "con trai của các con trai" would read as a riddle, and the meaning is the same.

source.text: וַיָּ֛מָת עַבְדּ֥וֹן בֶּן־הִלֵּ֖ל הַפִּרְעָתוֹנִ֑י וַיִּקָּבֵ֤ר בְּפִרְעָתוֹן֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּהַ֖ר הָעֲמָלֵקִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And died Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite and was buried at Pirathon in [the] land of Ephraim, in [the] hill country of the Amalekite[s].

en.L: And Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekite.
en.B: Then Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
en.R: Then Abdon died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim. It was in the hills that had once belonged to the Amalekites.

sw.L: Naye Abdoni mwana wa Hileli Mpirathoni akafa, akazikwa Pirathoni katika nchi ya Efraimu, katika nchi ya milima ya Mwamaleki.
sw.B: Kisha Abdoni mwana wa Hileli Mpirathoni alikufa, akazikwa Pirathoni katika nchi ya Efraimu, katika nchi ya milima ya Waamaleki.
sw.R: Kisha Abdoni alikufa, akazikwa Pirathoni katika nchi ya Efraimu. Ilikuwa katika milima iliyokuwa mali ya Waamaleki zamani.

es.L: Y murió Abdón hijo de Hilel, el piratonita, y fue sepultado en Piratón, en la tierra de Efraín, en la región montañosa del amalecita.
es.B: Después Abdón hijo de Hilel, el piratonita, murió y fue sepultado en Piratón, en la tierra de Efraín, en la región montañosa de los amalecitas.
es.R: Después Abdón murió y fue sepultado en Piratón, en la tierra de Efraín. Estaba en la región montañosa que antes había pertenecido a los amalecitas.

fr.L: Et Abdôn, fils de Hillel, le Piratonite, mourut et fut enterré à Piratôn, dans le pays d’Éphraïm, dans la montagne de l’Amalécite.
fr.B: Puis Abdôn, fils de Hillel, le Piratonite, mourut, et il fut enterré à Piratôn, dans le pays d’Éphraïm, dans la montagne des Amalécites.
fr.R: Puis Abdôn est mort, et on l’a enterré à Piratôn, dans le pays d’Éphraïm. C’était dans les collines qui avaient autrefois appartenu aux Amalécites.

vi.L: Áp-đôn con trai Hi-lên, người Phi-ra-thôn, qua đời và được chôn tại Phi-ra-thôn trong xứ Ép-ra-im, trên vùng đồi núi của người A-ma-léc.
vi.B: Rồi Áp-đôn con trai Hi-lên, người Phi-ra-thôn, qua đời và được chôn tại Phi-ra-thôn trong xứ Ép-ra-im, trên vùng đồi núi của người A-ma-léc.
vi.R: Rồi Áp-đôn qua đời và được chôn tại Phi-ra-thôn trong xứ Ép-ra-im. Nơi ấy ở trong vùng đồi núi trước kia thuộc về người A-ma-léc.

ko.L: 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들 압돈이 죽어 에브라임 땅 아말렉 사람의 산지에 있는 비라돈에 묻혔다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 비라돈 사람 힐렐의 아들 압돈은 죽어서 에브라임 땅, 아말렉 사람들의 산지에 있는 비라돈에 묻혔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 압돈은 죽어서 에브라임 땅에 있는 비라돈에 묻혔다. 그곳은 전에 아말렉 사람들이 살던 산지였다.

decisions.choice: the hill country of the Amalekites: a district in Ephraim named after Amalekites
decisions.reason: The Amalekites were desert raiders of the south (Exodus 17:8-16; Judges 6:3), but this hill district in Ephraim bore their name, perhaps because Amalekites had once lived there. The Song of Deborah also links Ephraim with Amalek (5:14). The reason for the name is not known.

decisions.choice: the Amalekite: a singular name standing for the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular with the article, "the Amalekite", meaning the Amalekite people as a group.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites; Readable "that had once belonged to"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the people. Readable adds "once belonged to" to explain the name; it is one likely reason, not a certain one.
